Expressed in head neurons; nerve ring; nervous system; tail neurons; and ventral cord neurons. Used to study alcohol use disorder. Is an ortholog of human UNC79 (unc-79 homolog, NALCN channel complex subunit).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: unc-79 encodes a novel, conserved protein; unc-79 functions in a pathway with unc-77 and nca-2, which encode alpha-1 subunits of voltage-insensitive cation leak channels, to regulate locomotion and the response to specific volatile anesthetics; unc-79 exerts its effects on these processes, at least in part, by regulating the levels of UNC-77 and NCA-2 proteins; an unc-79::gfp reporter is expressed in the nervous system in ventral nerve cord neurons in L2 and L3 larvae and in one or two head neurons in adults; UNC-79 exhibits a punctate staining pattern in ventral nerve cord and nerve ring processes, and this staining is dependent upon UNC-80, UNC-77, and NCA-2.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable clathrin binding activity. Involved in receptor-mediated endocytosis. Predicted to be located in intracellular membrane-bounded organelle and vesicle. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in Parkinson's disease 19A. Is an ortholog of human DNAJC6 (DnaJ heat shock protein family (Hsp40) member C6).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: The dnj-25 (Ce-auxilin) gene is required in vivo for clathrin-mediated endocytosis and for normal development.
Narrative: An upstream variant in dnj-25 could change expression of an auxilin required for endocytosis; misregulated endocytosis can alter receptor levels or signaling asymmetry in AMso and block neuronal fate acquisition [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact=MODIFIER; QUAL=23.7; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="dnj-25 required for clathrin-mediated endocytosis"].
rationale: DNJ-25 (auxilin) is required for clathrin-mediated endocytosis and receptor trafficking; altered trafficking can disrupt signaling asymmetries that determine AMso daughter fates.

WB_Overview: Predicted to be part of Cul2-RING ubiquitin ligase complex.
Narrative: A missense in gadr-2 might perturb components of a Cul2 ubiquitin ligase complex, altering degradation of polarity or fate-specifying proteins and thereby affecting AMso division outcomes [Effect=missense_variant; impact=MODERATE; QUAL=6.7; WB_Overview="predicted part of Cul2-RING ubiquitin ligase complex"].
rationale: GADR-2 is predicted to be part of a Cul2 ubiquitin ligase complex; ubiquitylation controls levels of fate determinants and polarity proteins, making it a plausible contributor if altered.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable ribosomal protein S6 kinase activity. Predicted to be involved in TORC1 signaling. Predicted to be located in cytoplasm and nucleoplasm. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in Coffin-Lowry syndrome; alcohol-related birth defects; and non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability 19. Is an ortholog of several human genes including RPS6KA1 (ribosomal protein S6 kinase A1); RPS6KA2 (ribosomal protein S6 kinase A2); and RPS6KA3 (ribosomal protein S6 kinase A3).
Narrative: A missense in rskn-1 (S6 kinase family) could alter growth and signaling pathways that interface with chromatin regulators or fate determinants, potentially perturbing AMso asymmetric division indirectly [Effect=missense_variant; impact=MODERATE; QUAL=7.6; WB_Overview="predicted ribosomal S6 kinase activity; involved in TORC1 signaling"; user_annotation: chromatin].
rationale: RSKN-1 is a kinase predicted to participate in TORC1 signaling and has been annotated to chromatin roles, so missense changes could alter growth-signaling or chromatin states that influence differentiation.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable transmembrane transporter activity. Predicted to be involved in chloride transmembrane transport and sulfate transmembrane transport. Predicted to be located in plasma membrane. Expressed in body wall musculature; excretory cell; hypodermis; intestine; and neurons.
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: sulp-1 encodes one of eight C. elegans members of the sulfate permease family of anion transporters; by homology, SULP-1 is predicted to function as an anion transporter that regulates cellular pH and volume via transmembrane movement of electrolytes and fluids; a sulp-1::GFP transcriptional fusion is expressed strongly in several neurons, weakly in hypodermal cells and the intestine, and very faintly in the excretory cell and body wall muscle.
Narrative: A missense in sulp-1, an anion transporter expressed in neurons, could change local ionic microenvironments or neuronal signaling required for AMso daughter fate bias, though direct evidence is limited [Effect=missense_variant; impact=MODERATE; QUAL=8.9; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="sulp-1 encodes a sulfate permease expressed in neurons"].
rationale: SULP-1 is a neuronal sulfate permease; altered ionic homeostasis or signaling can indirectly affect cell division orientation or signaling environment during AMso maturation.
